papers.title: Cu-N 4 Single-Atom Nanozyme with Multi-Enzyme Mimetic Activities Combined with In 2 O 3 /Bi 24 O 31 Br 10 Heterojunction: Toward Sensitive Triple-Mode Detection and Photocatalytic Inactivation of Vibrio Alginolyticus.
papers.abstract: In this study, a novel triple-mode biosensor based on a Cu-N 4 single-atom nanozyme (Cu-N 4 SAzyme) and an In 2 O 3 /Bi 24 O 31 Br 10 Z-Scheme heterojunction was constructed for the highly sensitive detection and photocatalytic inactivation of Vibrio alginolyticus (V. alginolyticus). The Cu-N 4 SAzyme, possessing both ascorbate oxidase-like and laccase-like activities, was integrated with nucleic acid isothermal amplification technology. This integration enabled triple-mode detection via photoelectrochemical (PEC), organic photoelectrochemical transistor biosensor (OPECT), and colorimetric (CL) methods, achieving a limit of detection (LOD, calculated) as low as 1.07 CFU/mL. An In 2 O 3 /Bi 24 O 31 Br 10 Z-Scheme heterojunction was fabricated as a photoactive gate electrode. Through UV-vis diffuse reflectance spectrum -, Mott-Schottky, and electron spin resonance analyses, we conclude that the electron transfer mechanism is consistent with the proposed Z-scheme mechanism, demonstrating that this structure exhibits highly efficient space charge separation and long carrier lifetime. Consequently, the photocurrent response was significantly enhanced, enabling highly sensitive triplex biosensing. Concurrently, the In 2 O 3 /Bi 24 O 31 Br 10 heterojunction was demonstrated to generate reactive oxygen species (ROS) under light irradiation, enabling the inactivation of a high concentration of V. alginolyticus (approximately 10 7.24 CFU/mL) within 3 h. This platform provides an integrated new strategy for both pathogen detection and disinfection.

papers.title: GPCRAgent: an intelligent multi-agent platform integrating knowledge graphs and large language models for GPCR-targeted drug discovery.
papers.abstract: G protein-coupled receptors (GPCRs) are major therapeutic targets in drug discovery. However, systematic characterization of GPCR functions and ligand interactions remains constrained by the high cost and complexity of experimental approaches. Although large language models (LLMs) have shown strong performance in biomedical question answering, their direct application to GPCR research is limited by insufficient integration of structured domain knowledge and poor interpretability of generated inferences. This study aimed to develop an interpretable artificial intelligence framework for automated and traceable analysis of complex GPCR-related problems, and to evaluate its utility in GPCR knowledge reasoning, structural property interpretation, disease target prioritization and ligand recommendation. We developed GPCRAgent, a multi-agent artificial intelligence framework enabled by VecKG-CoReason, which integrates vector-based semantic retrieval with knowledge graph-guided collaborative reasoning. GPCRAgent was evaluated on benchmark tasks covering GPCR knowledge question answering, multiple-choice reasoning and structural property interpretation. Its practical utility was further assessed in an idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis case study, in which prioritized targets and ligand candidates were supported by molecular docking and molecular dynamics simulations. GPCRAgent achieved accuracies of 85 % in GPCR knowledge question answering, 90 % in multiple-choice reasoning and 83 % in structural property interpretation, outperforming general-purpose LLMs across benchmark tasks. In an idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis case study, GPCRAgent identified LPAR1 as the top candidate and prioritized potential ligands. In a separate renal fibrosis study, experimental evaluation of the optimized LPAR1 ligand in kidney organoids showed suppressed fibrosis-associated marker induction during IL-1β-induced fibrosis. These results illustrate how the platform integrates evidence for target prioritization and structure-based ligand assessment. To facilitate broader adoption, an online platform (https://cbcb.cdutcm.edu.cn/GPCRAgent/) was developed to support GPCR-related drug discovery. By integrating structured knowledge retrieval with collaborative multi-agent reasoning, GPCRAgent provides an interpretable AI framework for evidence-based GPCR target prioritization, ligand recommendation, and decision support.

papers.title: Effects of exercise preconditioning on neuroinflammatory and neuroprotective markers in animal models of stroke: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
papers.abstract: Currently, mounting evidence suggests that exercise preconditioning beneficially modulates the neuroimmune responses following stroke. However, meta-analysis of preclinical studies specifically addressing this topic remain limited. This study aims to conduct a comprehensive analysis of preclinical literature investigating the effects of exercise preconditioning on neuroimmune responses in animal models of stroke. The objective is to provide a theoretical foundation and scientific rationale for applying exercise training in stroke prevention. PubMed, Web of Science, Embase, CNKI, Wanfang, and VIP were searched from inception to 20 July 2026 for randomized controlled trials (RCTs) that examined the effect of exercise preconditioning on neuroimmune responses after stroke in animal models. Effect sizes were pooled with a random-effects model and reported as standardized mean differences (SMD). A total of 24 studies were included in this systematic review. Meta-analysis revealed that in post-stroke brain tissue, exercise-pretreated animals exhibited significantly reduced levels of ionized calcium binding adapter molecule 1 (Iba1) [SMD = -2.85, 95% confidence interval (CI) (-4.66, -1.03)], interleukin (IL)-1β [SMD = -3.86, 95% CI (-5.73, -1.99)], IL-6 [SMD = -1.55, 95% CI (-2.98, -0.12)], inducible nitric oxide synthase (iNOS) [SMD = -6.18, 95% CI (-8.37, -3.99)], toll-like receptor 4 (TLR4) [SMD = -3.70, 95% CI (-5.28, -2.12)], nuclear transcription factor-κB (NF-κB) [SMD = -3.37, 95% CI (-4.59, -2.16)], Cysteine-dependent Aspartate-specific Protease-1 (Caspase-1) [SMD = -2.42, 95% CI (-3.70, -1.15)], and NLR family, pyrin domain containing protein 3 (NLRP3) [SMD = -2.77, 95% CI (-4.00, -1.53)] compared to non-exercising animals, while levels of IL-10 [SMD = 6.63, 95% CI (1.50, 11.75)], tyrosine kinase receptor B (TrkB) [SMD = 4.30, 95% CI (3.14, 5.46)], and neuronal nuclei antigen (NeuN) [SMD = 8.52, 95% CI (5.61, 11.44)] were significantly elevated. In serum, levels of tumor necrosis factor-α (TNF-α) [SMD = -4.50, 95% CI (-7.66, -1.34)] and IL-1β [SMD = -2.41, 95% CI (-3.49, -1.32)] were significantly reduced. No significant differences were observed in other neuroimmune responses. Exercise preconditioning appears to exert beneficial effects on neuroinflammatory and neuroprotective markers after experimental stroke. Nevertheless, the certainty of the evidence is limited by small sample sizes, substantial heterogeneity, unclear risk of bias across multiple domains, potential small-study effects, and the predominance of young male animals. Therefore, these findings should be interpreted with caution and require confirmation in rigorously designed preclinical studies.

papers.title: Finding the missing millions with tuberculosis.
papers.abstract: Tuberculosis remains the world's leading cause of death from a single microbial pathogen. Approximately 2.4 million of an estimated 10.7 million annual cases are still missed. In order to achieve a substantial decrease of the global tuberculosis burden earlier, broader, and more accessible case detection is required. A major challenge is that roughly half of people with bacteriologically confirmed tuberculosis report no symptoms, highlighting the importance of symptom-agnostic screening and active case finding. Recent guidance by the World Health Organization has expanded diagnostic options, including chest radiography, C-reactive protein, rapid molecular tests, concurrent testing of different specimen types, and new near-point-of-care nucleic acid amplification tests. Alternative, non-sputum specimens such as tongue swabs, stool, urine, exhaled breath, and blood may improve access for children, people living with HIV, and individuals with paucibacillary or early disease. However, many emerging technologies still lack sufficient real-world performance. Ultimately, diagnostic innovation alone will not reduce the burden of tuberculosis. Effective implementation must be combined with action on poverty, malnutrition, healthcare access, and other social determinants to convert scientific progress into population-level impact, particularly across high-burden and resource-constrained settings.

papers.title: Visual Detection of Foodborne Viruses in Leafy Greens Using an AsCas12f-Split-G-Quadruplex Sensor.
papers.abstract: Foodborne viruses are responsible for a substantial burden of disease worldwide, with fresh produce serving as the most abundant vehicle for transmission. However, rapid detection in solid produce, such as leafy greens, remains underdeveloped, as conventional methods often require labor-intensive sample preparation and specialized instrumentation. Herein, we present a colorimetric CRISPR-split-G4 biosensor for rapid viral surveillance in leafy greens that combines reverse transcription recombinase polymerase amplification (RT-RPA), AsCas12f-mediated trans-cleavage, and a modular split-G-quadruplex (split-G4) reporter system. In this system, target recognition activates the trans-cleavage activity of AsCas12f, resulting in degradation of a blocker strand and subsequent assembly of a catalytically active G4-hemin DNAzyme that generates a visible signal easily detectable by the naked eye. Using norovirus as a model pathogen, the platform exhibited high analytical sensitivity and specificity, enabling reliable detection of viral particles with minimal instrumentation. To evaluate practical applicability, the assay was coupled with a simplified leaf-disk extraction workflow and successfully applied to contaminated romaine lettuce and baby spinach samples without requiring viral nucleic acid purification. The platform achieved detection limits of 1000 and 5000 viral copies per 100 mg of romaine lettuce and spinach tissue, respectively. From sample processing to visual readout, the entire assay was completed in approximately 2 h. By integrating isothermal amplification, CRISPR-based target recognition, and instrument-free signal generation into a streamlined workflow, this strategy provides a promising platform for decentralized food safety monitoring and establishes a flexible framework for the on-site detection of viral pathogens in complex food matrices.

papers.title: Impact of multiplex PCR respiratory panels on antimicrobial stewardship and clinical outcomes in hospitalized adults with pneumonia: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
papers.abstract: Inadequate empiric antimicrobial therapy increases mortality and healthcare costs. Rapid multiplex PCR respiratory panels can provide faster and more sensitive pathogen detection than conventional culture-based methods; however, interpretation may be limited by detection of colonizing organisms and resistance genes that do not always correspond to phenotypic resistance. Their impact on clinical outcomes and antimicrobial stewardship remains uncertain due to heterogeneous studies and clinical implementation strategies. This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluates the clinical value of these panels in hospitalized adults with pneumonia. Following PRISMA guidelines, we searched MEDLINE, EMBASE, and the Cochrane Library through October 15, 2025, for randomized controlled trials (RCTs) comparing multiplex PCR-guided therapy with standard microbiological testing. The primary outcome was total antibiotic duration. Secondary outcomes included incidence of targeted/appropriate antimicrobial therapy, length of hospitalization, 1-month mortality, 1-month hospital readmission, and antibiotic-related adverse events. The analysis included six RCTs involving 2,087 patients. Multiplex PCR-guided therapy showed a modest but non-significant reduction in antibiotic duration (MD -0.74 days; 95% CI: -2.28 to 0.79; p = 0.22). No statistically significant differences were found for secondary outcomes, including targeted or appropriate antimicrobial therapy, length of hospitalization, antibiotic-related adverse events, 1-month mortality, or 1-month hospital readmissions. Multiplex PCR panels provide rapid diagnostic data, but the available randomized evidence provides insufficient evidence that their implementation reduces total antibiotic duration or downstream clinical outcomes in patients with pneumonia. These findings do not exclude potential benefits in earlier antimicrobial optimization, which appear to depend on clinical context and implementation strategy.

papers.title: Global population-based prevalence of genetic carriers of CDH1-associated hereditary diffuse gastric cancer.
papers.abstract: Hereditary diffuse gastric cancer (HDGC) is a rare autosomal dominant genetic disorder caused by loss-of-function mutations in the tumor suppressor gene CDH1. We aimed to estimate the carrier prevalence of HDGC-associated CDH1 variants across genetic ancestry groups using a large genomic database to identify potential disparities. We conducted a population-based cross-sectional analysis of 807,162 unrelated individuals in gnomAD v4.1 across diverse genetic ancestry groups. CDH1 variants were identified using two approaches: (1) pathogenic or likely pathogenic (P/LP) variants classified by ClinVar or ClinGen, and (2) additional rare variants predicted to be deleterious in silico, including nonsense, frameshift, deleterious in-frame indels, splice-disrupting, and supported missense variants. Carrier frequency was estimated from combined allele frequencies and stratified by genetic ancestry. Among 3,381 CDH1 variants, 137 met study criteria. 47 were classified as P/LP by ClinVar or ClinGen, and 90 additional variants were predicted to be deleterious in silico. Using curated P/LP variants, the overall estimated carrier frequency was 8.67 per 100,000 individuals, with the highest ancestry-specific estimate in non-Finnish Europeans at 10.0 per 100,000. No carriers were observed in Ashkenazi Jewish, Finnish, or Middle Eastern groups. Inclusion of in silico-predicted variants increased the estimated carrier frequency to 44.1 per 100,000, with the highest estimate in the Middle Eastern group at 165.0 per 100,000. HDGC-associated CDH1 variants may be more broadly distributed across populations than previously recognized. This genotype-first approach provides population-level carrier estimates independent of clinical ascertainment and highlights ancestry-related variation requiring further clinical and functional validation.

papers.title: Rare genetic variants in leber hereditary optic neuropathy: molecular mechanisms, diagnosis, and emerging therapies.
papers.abstract: Hereditary optic neuropathies, such as Leber's hereditary optic neuropathy (LHON), remain a focus of active research. Diagnostic challenges and severe clinical consequences often result in atypical presentations, creating significant obstacles for neuro-ophthalmology. The field has garnered increased attention due to advances in molecular biology and genetic engineering. Pathogenic variants in mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA) and nuclear DNA disrupt oxidative phosphorylation, reduce adenosine triphosphate production, and increase reactive oxygen species generation, to which retinal ganglion cells are particularly vulnerable. Rare genetic variants have been identified in LHON and related mitochondrial disorders, including mitochondrial encephalomyopathy, lactic acidosis, and stroke-like episodes and Leigh syndrome. Phenotypic heterogeneity, variable heteroplasmy levels, and limited sensitivity of targeted genetic testing complicate the detection and interpretation of rare variants. As a result, comprehensive next-generation sequencing is increasingly necessary for accurate molecular diagnosis and timely treatment initiation. Recent therapeutic interventions include genotype-specific approaches, such as adeno-associated virus serotype 2-mediated allotopic expression, and genotype-independent therapies, such as idebenone. Diagnostic standards for mitochondrial optic neuropathies have shifted from focusing solely on the three primary pathogenic mtDNA variants to a broader molecular diagnostic framework. Future research should prioritize mtDNA sequencing in cases with inconclusive diagnoses using conventional methods, incorporate mitochondrial and nuclear genomics, and leverage artificial intelligence-based approaches. Accurate identification and classification of rare variants, together with a deeper understanding of their phenotypic consequences, will facilitate the development of individualized therapeutic strategies to prevent further visual decline. This review outlines potential directions for multifaceted treatment strategies in patients with rare LHON-associated variants and critically evaluates current evidence regarding the clinical significance of rare mitochondrial and nuclear genetic variants in LHON and related mitochondrial optic neuropathies.

papers.title: Systematic Profiling of Encoder Architectures and Multimodal Embeddings in Protein Foundation Models Reveals Data Set-Driven Separability Regimes in Prediction of Allosteric and Orthosteric Binding Sites.
papers.abstract: Allosteric regulation represents a fundamental mechanism of protein function, yet distinguishing allosteric from orthosteric protein-binding sites remains a persistent computational challenge. While multimodal protein foundation models offer the potential to integrate complementary biological signals, including sequence, structure, functional annotations, and conformational dynamics, their performance determinants in allosteric binding site detection remain poorly understood. We introduce a unified computational framework for profiling multimodal protein foundation models across distinct binding site separability regimes. Rather than evaluating models solely by predictive accuracy, the framework combines systematic modality embedding ablations, encoder architecture comparisons, and variance decomposition to characterize how evolutionary, structural, functional, and dynamical information contributes to allosteric site discrimination. Using the OneProt multimodal model, we evaluate two complementary levels of multimodal integration: (a) encoder architectures that differ in the modalities incorporated during pretraining and (b) downstream combinations of pocket, sequence, and text embeddings used for classification. To systematically probe the determinants of model performance, we benchmark these configurations across four assembled data sets of protein complexes representing a spectrum of biological complexity and a range of structural, dynamic, and evolutionary contexts for orthosteric and allosteric binding sites. Through comprehensive embedding ablations, encoder architecture comparisons, and variance decomposition, we demonstrate that model performance is governed primarily by intrinsic data set properties rather than architectural complexity, with data set identity accounting for 63.7% of explainable variance. Across the data sets examined, we identify substantial differences not only in overall separability but also in the information accessible from different pretrained representations. Single-modality controls show that high predictive performance does not necessarily imply reliance on the explicitly provided pocket representation: depending on data set composition, substantial discrimination can already be obtained from sequence- or text-based multimodal representations. Within-protein comparisons nevertheless demonstrate that pocket-containing representations retain binding site-specific discriminatory information when protein identity and the associated sequence and text representations are held constant. At the encoder level, structural and molecular dynamics encoders provide the greatest benefit in intermediate and high separability settings. Example-level analysis further shows that combining data sets can reshape which binding sites are preferentially recognized. These findings establish that the success of multimodal foundation models depends critically on alignment between available modalities and the biological signatures that distinguish regulatory classes in each data set.

papers.title: Draft genome sequences of two Stenotrophomonas muris isolates, CBAS 1154 and CBAS 1234, recovered from patients with ICU-acquired ventilator-associated sepsis.
papers.abstract: We report the high-quality draft genome sequences of two clinical Stenotrophomonas muris isolates recovered from the lower respiratory tract of intensive care unit patients with ventilator-associated sepsis in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil. Based on our review of the available literature, we found no previous records of this species from Brazil.
authors: Isabel Ribeiro Gomes de Queiroz Crespo

papers.title: Spatially integrated transcriptomics maps the metastatic niche in lymph nodes of gastric cancer.
papers.abstract: Lymph node (LN) metastasis is a major determinant of clinical outcome in gastric cancer (GC), yet the molecular and spatial features of metastatic LN niches remain incompletely defined. Here, we integrated digital spatial profiling (DSP) of primary GC and matched LNs, single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq), and 10x Genomics Visium spatial transcriptomics. Cross-sectional analysis of cytokeratin-positive regions across primary GC and N1-N3 metastatic lymph nodes (mLNs) identified a hybrid epithelial-mesenchymal expression pattern in N1 samples and prominent immune checkpoint, angiogenic, and receptor tyrosine kinase programs in the N3 group. Deconvolution showed enrichment of exhausted T cells, regulatory T cells, and fibroblasts in mLNs, consistent with immunosuppressive remodeling of the local microenvironment. Cell-cell communication analysis implicated the galectin-9 (LGALS9)-CD45/CD44, CLEC2D-KLRB1, and CCL19/CCL21-CCR7 axes in mLNs. Spatial analysis further revealed compartment-specific heterogeneity, including distinct proliferative, immune, and immunosuppressive programs. Integrating multiple transcriptomic datasets, we derived a 12-gene lymph node metastasis gene signature (LNMGS); high LNMGS scores were associated with poorer overall survival in the TCGA-STAD cohort. Spatial mapping of the LNMGS in primary GC identified an LNMGS-high region displaying a center-to-periphery expression gradient and tending to have a higher inferred copy-number burden. A distance-associated gene signature derived from this gradient was enriched for proliferation, invasion, angiogenesis, immune evasion, and stemness. Together, these findings provide a spatial and molecular framework for lymph node metastasis in GC and highlight potential biomarkers and therapeutic targets for further investigation. © 2026 The Pathological Society of Great Britain and Ireland.

papers.title: Unified Command in Local Public Health: Case Studies of Rabies and Tuberculosis Responses in Douglas County, Nebraska.
papers.abstract: As public health emergencies become more frequent and complex, local health departments must increasingly rely on public-private partnerships and whole-community approaches to respond effectively. The Douglas County Health Department (DCHD), serving Nebraska's most populous county, demonstrates how a local agency can coordinate large-scale responses by implementing a unified command structure with diverse partners. This case study presents 2 concurrent public health emergencies that occurred in late 2023: (1) the detection of raccoon rabies virus variant (RRVV) in a domestic kitten, a pathogen not previously identified in Nebraska, and (2) the largest pediatric tuberculosis (TB) exposure investigated in the county's history. Both incidents required rapid coordination across local, state, and federal agencies, as well as engagement with healthcare systems and community organizations. In each response, DCHD activated a unified command structure to facilitate operational objectives, allocate resources, and coordinate risk communication. The rabies response included enhanced animal surveillance, a trap-vaccinate-release campaign, and the manual distribution of 18,000 oral rabies vaccine baits. No additional human or animal cases of RRVV were identified. The TB response involved identifying 643 exposed individuals, conducting mass testing clinics with local healthcare partners, and rapidly initiating prophylaxis for vulnerable populations. No cases of secondary transmission were identified. These case studies demonstrate how local health departments can lead complex responses by leveraging established partnerships, aligning with National Incident Management System principles, and coordinating unified command operations. Lessons learned from Douglas County's experience offer practical guidance for other jurisdictions preparing for zoonotic and airborne infectious disease threats, especially when internal resources are limited.

papers.title: Postmortem pulmonary concentrations of tilmicosin and gamithromycin in cattle with fatal bovine respiratory disease.
papers.abstract: Bovine respiratory disease (BRD) is a health and economic problem in intensive beef production. Antimicrobial (ATM) therapy requires adequate ATM concentrations at the pulmonary infection site. This study determined pulmonary concentrations of tilmicosin (TIL) and gamithromycin (GAM) in cattle that died from BRD under field conditions and characterized the ATM susceptibility of isolates recovered from affected lungs. Lung samples from 41 cattle were analyzed by liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry. TIL was detected in 56.1% of lungs (0.013-8.811 µg/g; mean 0.956 µg/g; median 0.117 µg/g), and GAM in 24.4% (0.032-2.323 µg/g; mean 0.570 µg/g; median 0.193 µg/g). Detection of TIL and GAM was significantly associated with reported treatment (p<0.001); in animals with documented treatment, TIL and GAM were detected in 90% and 100% of cases, respectively. Concentrations varied widely between animals and were lower than those previously reported in healthy cattle. This may point to altered pulmonary ATM accumulation in advanced BRD; however, the observational design, without a healthy or survivor comparison group or paired plasma measurements, does not allow this explanation to be established. Susceptibility testing of 46 evaluable isolates showed 93.5% and 97.8% susceptibility to TIL and GAM, respectively. Despite this susceptibility, the animals died; the data cannot establish the cause, which may involve disease stage at treatment, timing of diagnosis, irreversible lung injury, pathogen interactions, host factors, or altered pulmonary ATM distribution. The findings emphasize the need to integrate knowledge of pulmonary ATM distribution, early diagnosis, and rational ATM use to improve BRD outcomes.

papers.title: A one-step LAMP-CRISPR/Cas12a platform targeting lytA and cpsA for rapid parallel identification and virulence stratification of Streptococcus pneumoniae .
papers.abstract: Streptococcus pneumoniae ( S. pneumoniae , SPN) is the primary pathogen causing community-acquired pneumonia (CAP), purulent meningitis, sepsis, and acute otitis media. Accurate species identification and rapid differentiation of invasive strains are critical for clinical management and infection control. Based on loop-mediated isothermal amplification (LAMP) and CRISPR/Cas12a technologies, this study established a parallel dual-target detection platform targeting the S. pneumoniae -specific lytA gene and the capsular polysaccharide synthesis regulatory gene cpsA . A dual-readout mode combining fluorescence detection (FD) and lateral flow test strip (LFTS) was adopted to meet diverse laboratory testing requirements. For each target-specific reaction, LAMP amplification and CRISPR/Cas12a cleavage were sequentially performed in a single closed tube using paraffin-oil stratification to suppress solvent evaporation, effectively preventing aerosol contamination. Range-finding serial-dilution assays revealed that the lowest gDNA concentrations producing positive signals in all three technical replicates reached 1 fg μL -1 (FD) and 10 fg μL -1 (LFTS). This assay specifically distinguished S. pneumoniae from other common clinical pathogens and preliminarily identified encapsulated invasive strains, with 100% sensitivity and specificity consistent with conventional PCR. This LAMP-CRISPR/Cas12a platform, with its closed-tube design, avoids contamination, while FD and LFTS dual readouts cater to diverse testing needs. Featuring high sensitivity, excellent specificity, simplicity, and speed, it provides an innovative and practical solution for the rapid diagnosis of S. pneumoniae and holds great clinical potential.

papers.title: Characterization of a Fungal Modular Polyketide Synthase System Reveals an Unusual Strategy for Polyketide Chain Initiation.
papers.abstract: Polyketides constitute a major class of natural products with remarkable structural diversity and biological activities. While bacteria predominantly produce polyketides via modular type I polyketide synthases (PKSs), eukaryotic modular PKSs remain largely unexplored. Here, we report the functional characterization of a fungal modular PKS system from Lasiodiplodia theobromae through heterologous expression in Aspergillus oryzae, leading to the production of the antimalarial macrolide strasseriolide C (1). Intriguingly, biosynthesis of 1 involves C-methylation of the starter malonyl unit despite the absence of a methyltransferase domain in the loading module. Furthermore, module 2 of the PKS system contains an unusual arrangement of four consecutive acyl carrier protein (ACP) domains. Although the catalytic basis of this methylation remains unresolved, our isotope-labeling experiments, mutational analyses, and in vitro biochemical assays support a model in which the malonyl unit loaded onto the module 2 ACPs is transferred to the loading ACP, where starter-unit methylation is proposed to occur prior to chain initiation. Our study reveals unexpected biosynthetic logic and establishes a foundation for mechanistic studies and engineering of eukaryotic modular PKSs.

papers.title: A single-cell transcriptomic atlas of the pigtail macaque lung
papers.abstract: Background: The lungs undergo substantial physiological and immunological changes during respiratory illness to meet the host's increased metabolic and oxygen demands. These responses require coordination among epithelial, endothelial, stromal, and immune cells throughout the respiratory zone, interstitium, and vasculature. Nonhuman primates (NHPs) are a valuable model for studying pulmonary biology as they have similar anatomic, physiologic, and immunologic correspondence to humans. Despite the widespread use of NHPs in pulmonary research, the cellular diversity and molecular characteristics of the pigtail macaque lung remain incompletely defined. Methods: Parenchymal lung tissue from five adult female pigtail macaques (Macaca nemestrina) was dissociated into single cells and profiled using 10x Genomics 3' single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-Seq). Next, ambient RNA was removed and quality control analyses performed. Samples were then integrated using scVI and scANVI. Cell types were labeled after unsupervised clustering and subclustering, followed by manual annotation using canonical marker genes. We compared lineages and cell types with the Level 4 Human Lung Cell Atlas (HLCA) using scArches reference mapping and with the Rhesus Immune Reference Atlas (RIRA) using Seurat label transfer. Results: The atlas includes 61,323 cells representing 37 cell types in epithelial, mesenchymal, endothelial, lymphoid, and myeloid populations. Annotated populations included both major and rare lung cell types, including alveolar type I and II cells, club and multiciliated cells, aerocyte capillary, and lymphatic endothelial cells, pre-terminal bronchiole secretory cells, CD4+ and CD8+ T cells, and several innate-like lymphocyte populations (gamma delta T cells, MAIT-like cells, innate-like CD8+ T cells, and group 3 innate lymphoid cells). There was strong concordance at HLCA annotation level 4, including AT1 and AT2 cells (96% and 93%), B cells (94 to 97%), CD4+ T cells (99 to 100%), classical and non-classical monocytes (84% and 85%), alveolar macrophages (80%), and mast cells (96%). Immune populations mapped to the RIRA with similar fidelity (alveolar macrophages and B cells, 99%). Conclusions: While studies of pandemic respiratory infections, vaccines, and therapeutics rely on NHP disease models, this atlas provides a unique reference for epithelial, endothelial, stromal, and immune cell states in the pigtail macaque lung. We found that single-cell populations from the pigtail macaque lung are highly similar to those in the human lung at the lineage level. This reference will enable studies of pathogenesis and vaccine and drug efficacy in a highly translational model of the human lung.

papers.title: GeneEmbedLLM: Harnessing Large Language Models for Gene Functional Embedding and Association Prediction
papers.abstract: Effective and high-quality gene function representations are crucial for bioinformatics tasks. While biological knowledge about genes is inherently textual, encompassing functional descriptions and pathway annotations, current methods often rely on single-source, non-textual data, failing to capture the rich semantic information in multi-source gene annotations. In this paper, we propose GeneEmbedLLM, a Large Language Model (LLM)-powered framework for generating universal, semantically-aware gene embeddings. The proposed approach advances the gene representation learning through multi-source structured text integration from five authoritative databases and attribute-aware attention based on Longformer architecture and contrastive learning. Experimental results on diverse downstream tasks, ranging from molecular interactions and phenotypic dependencies to epigenetic regulation, confirm the validity and effectiveness of our proposed approach, where competitive performance is achieved across all evaluated benchmarks. We further validate the quality of the generated embeddings through comprehensive analyses, including embedding visualizations, intra-pathway similarity assessments, ablation study, and parameter analysis.

papers.title: Integrating bacterial genomics and host transcriptomics links Burkholderia pseudomallei variation to melioidosis mortality and neutrophil responses
papers.abstract: Bacterial genetic variation contributes to the outcome of infection, but its relationship with host immune responses is rarely investigated in the same patients, limiting the biological interpretation of pathogen-associated disease severity. Here, we integrated pathogen genomics, clinical outcomes and host transcriptomics to investigate host-pathogen interactions in melioidosis, a frequently fatal infection caused by Burkholderia pseudomallei. We analysed prospective clinical data from 2,142 patients, whole-genome sequences from 2,101 infecting isolates and 646 paired host blood transcriptomes across five cohorts collected between 2012 and 2023. Infections were typically dominated by a single strain, with limited within-host diversification, supporting the use of an infecting isolate genome to investigate pathogen-associated clinical outcomes. Bacterial genome-wide association studies identified one locus associated with binary mortality at genome-wide significance. Incorporating patient age, sex, body mass index and Charlson Comorbidity Index increased this to four, while modelling time to death as a continuous phenotype identified seven loci. Integration with paired host transcriptomes linked mortality-associated bacterial genetic variation to imputed signatures of increased immature neutrophils and reduced neutrophil degranulation. An intergenic region upstream of the polyketide synthesis locus BPSS1006-BPSS1011 was additionally associated with downregulation of host genes involved in myeloid-cell signalling and cell proliferation pathways. These findings connect naturally occurring B. pseudomallei genomic variation associated with mortality to distinct host immune signatures, providing insight into pathogen-host interactions underlying severe melioidosis and a framework for investigating the contribution of pathogen genetic diversity to clinical outcomes.

papers.title: Human medial frontal neurons represent integrated semantic content and sensory evidence to inform decision-making
papers.abstract: Humans can reconfigure how they act on the world from a single verbal instruction. Central to this capacity is the ability to represent what an instruction specifies and to bring that content to bear on incoming sensory evidence. However, little is known about where in the human brain instruction content is encoded, how it combines with sensory evidence to produce a choice, and how this integration relates to behavior. Here, we characterized single-neuron and population responses recorded in the ventral temporal cortex, medial temporal lobe, medial frontal cortex and ventromedial prefrontal cortex of neurosurgical patients performing a verbal instruction task. On each trial, a written instruction specified which stimulus feature was relevant and whether the correct response was to choose or to reject the stimulus that best matched it, so that the same image pair required opposite responses under different instructions. Only medial frontal populations jointly encoded the instructed task, and the target feature, whereas ventral temporal populations encoded stimulus features along axes that generalized across instruction conditions. Choice representation emerged first in ventromedial prefrontal and then in medial frontal cortex during stimulus presentation, before a motor response could be prepared. Shuffling instruction content selectively degraded prediction of medial frontal population activity, whereas shuffling stimulus identity selectively degraded ventral temporal activity. To ask how these representations could be computed, we trained a vision-language model with separable visual and linguistic streams converging on a recurrent decision module to perform the same task. Its visual embeddings predicted held-out ventral temporal activity and its recurrent activations revealed a task solution space that predicted medial frontal activity, and the strength of this alignment tracked behavioral accuracy. These results identify a cortical hierarchy in which medial frontal circuitry represents the content of verbal goals and acts on a ventral temporal substrate whose representational axes remain stable, and indicate that functional hierarchies discovered in artificial networks can serve as predictive models of human neural circuitry.

papers.title: MELD: Mutation Effect Learning through Differential embeddings
papers.abstract: We introduce MELD (Mutation Effect Learning through Differential Embeddings), a compact model for predicting the functional consequences of single nucleotide variants (SNVs) by training directly on the wild-type (WT) versus mutant differential. Interpreting SNVs is central to clinical genomics, yet experimental characterization cannot scale to millions of observed variants. Leading sequence-to-function models (Enformer, Borzoi, AlphaGenome) are trained on absolute genomic tracks and score variants post hoc through in-silico mutagenesis (ISM), so the WT-mutant difference never enters the training loss. MELD instead places the logit difference {Delta}z = zmut - zwt inside the supervised objective. It combines a shared CNN-Transformer encoder, a mutant-specific mutation-mask boost, multiscale mutation-centered pooling, and a learned adaptive amplification factor . On ClinVar (1.57M variants), MELD (1.9M parameters) reached an AUROC of 0.986 versus 0.800 for a same-data, same-backbone ISM baseline, with ablations confirming the contribution of each component. On a shared benchmark, it outperformed frozen foundation models with 3-1,300x more parameters (AUROC 0.967 vs. 0.924 for AlphaGenome and 0.936 for Nucleotide Transformer). With only 50, 000 training variants, it exceeded the ISM baseline trained on all 1.48M (AUROC 0.903 vs. 0.796) variants. On BRCA1 saturation genome editing, frozen MELD achieved a Spearman {rho} of 0.42, above Borzoi (0.40), and ClinVar transfer raised it to 0.45. These results demonstrate that direct differential supervision is a compact, data-efficient alternative to post-hoc ISM scoring with substantially larger pretrained models.

papers.title: Integrated Transcriptomic and Translatomic Profiling Reveals Noncanonical RNA Junctions and Hidden Coding Potential in Porcine Epidemic Diarrhea Virus
papers.abstract: Porcine epidemic diarrhea virus (PEDV) poses a major threat to the global swine industry. Although coronavirus discontinuous transcription is well characterized, the classical model cannot fully explain the diversity of viral RNA junctions, while conventional genome annotations may underestimate viral protein-coding capacity. To address these gaps, we integrated time-resolved RNA sequencing (RNA-seq), cycloheximide (CHX)- and harringtonine (HAR)-treated ribosome profiling (Ribo-seq), comparative genomics, and peptide mass spectrometry to investigate PEDV RNA expression and hidden coding potential. RNA-seq revealed that, at 3 hours post-infection (hpi), the 3 genomic region exhibited strong relative coverage enrichment, whereas the relative contribution of the 5 replicase-coding region increased rapidly between 3 and 5 hpi, suggesting a possible transition from sgRNA-dominated RNA accumulation toward enhanced genomic RNA replication. Genome-wide junction analysis identified 43,635 distinct noncanonical RNA junctions, although canonical sgRNA junctions accounted for 95.5% of all junction-supporting reads. Several abundant noncanonical sgRNAs were predicted to generate novel coding products, including N-x4, N-x2, M-x3, and M-x2, short peptides encoded within the 3 untranslated region (UTR), and two distinct N-terminally truncated S proteins, thereby expanding the potential coding repertoire of PEDV. Genome-wide reading-frame analysis uncovered a pronounced asymmetry in hidden coding potential, identifying 68 overlapping open reading frames (ORFs) longer than 40 amino acids in the +1 reading frame, compared with only three in the +2 frame. Ribo-seq further revealed a progressive redistribution of viral ribosome occupancy toward structural protein-coding regions during the later stages of infection. By integrating HAR-associated translation initiation-site enrichment with CHX-based ORF-level translation analysis, we identified several noncanonical ORFs with strong translation-associated evidence, including N-x1, N-x2, S-x1, and ORF1b-x13. Moreover, peptide mass spectrometry detected a characteristic peptide corresponding to N-x1 in infected samples, providing independent proteomic evidence for the expression of this previously unannotated viral protein. Together, these findings uncover extensive noncanonical RNA synthesis and hidden protein-coding capacity in PEDV, establishing a foundation for understanding novel viral gene expression strategies and their potential evolutionary and pathogenic significance.

papers.title: Preemptive SOD1 Silencing via Neonatal Intramuscular AAV Therapy Modifies Disease Trajectory in an ALS Mouse Model
papers.abstract: Amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) is a progressive and fatal neurodegenerative disorder with limited therapeutic options. A major challenge for developing effective therapies is the safe and efficient delivery of genetic cargo to the spinal motor neurons that degenerate in the disease. This is particularly pertinent for SOD1-linked familial ALS, where gene silencing approaches are promising but remain constrained by suboptimal delivery. Here, we establish a gene delivery platform that overcomes this barrier by combining the retrograde transport of rAAV2-retro with an artificial miRNA to achieve pan-spinal SOD1 silencing. A single intramuscular injection of rAAV2-retro-miRNA into neonatal SOD1G93A mice achieved widespread transduction of spinal motor neurons, significant reduction of mutant SOD1 protein, and conferred multifaceted therapeutic benefits. Treated mice exhibited delayed disease onset, extended lifespan, preserved motor function, reduced neuroinflammation, and protection of neuromuscular junctions and spinal motor neurons. These findings establish the rAAV2-retro-miRNA platform as a versatile and efficient tool for spinal motor neuron-targeted gene silencing, addressing the delivery challenge and providing a foundation for further development in motor neuron diseases.

papers.title: A Proteome-Wide Gain-of-Function Atlas Mapping the Landscape of Chemotherapy Response
papers.abstract: Background: Conventional chemotherapies remain the core therapeutic backbone of cancer treatment, yet the rapid emergence of chemoresistance often compromises their clinical efficacy. Although large-scale functional genomics has transformed precision oncology, existing reference maps rely predominantly on loss-of-function paradigms and lack systematic data on gain-of-function (GOF) events that commonly drive clinical resistance. Methods: To address this gap, we engineered a site-specific Bxb1 integrase landing-pad system in HeLa cells, enabling single-copy integration of a human proteome-wide library [18,388 open reading frames (ORFs)] at the AAVS1 locus under a uniform EF1 promoter. We systematically profiled cellular fitness across 16 chemotherapeutics. We integrated this GOF perturbation screen with bulk and single-cell RNA sequencing, FACS-based lysosomal functional screening, clinical cohort survival analyses, and preclinical xenograft modeling. Results: Stratified modeling of over 230,000 gene-drug interactions defined distinct functional categories that are strongly enriched for clinical cancer biomarkers and prognostic relevance. Global network analysis and organelle-specific lysosomal functional screening uncovered that chemotherapeutic agents, most prominently the nucleoside analog TAS-102 (Lonsurf), converge upon a shared survival hub centered on the BCL-2 family-associated autophagy-endolysosomal network. Mechanistically, TAS-102 triggered lysosomal activation as an adaptive survival response. Co-treatment with the BCL-2 family inhibitor ABT-263 (Navitoclax) attenuated this TAS-102-induced lysosomal response and synergistically reversed TAS-102 resistance across colorectal and pancreatic cancer models in vitro and in colorectal cell line- and patient-derived xenograft (CDX, PDX) models in vivo. Conclusions: Our study establishes an open-access, proteome-wide GOF reference atlas that systematically maps chemotherapeutic responses, recapitulates canonical resistance biology, and nominates rational drug combinations. This systems-genomics resource bridges massive-scale perturbation mapping with actionable target discovery, providing a translational framework to overcome therapeutic resistance and reprogram cancer drug responses.

papers.title: Functional genomics reveals mediators of beta cell survival in ER stress and type 2 diabetes risk
papers.abstract: Endoplasmic reticulum (ER) stress in pancreatic beta cells contributes to impaired function and type 2 diabetes (T2D). In this study we performed genome-wide perturbation screens and genomic profiling in beta cells to identify novel mediators of ER stress responses and diabetes risk. We defined gene regulatory networks in beta cells and identified specific beta cell networks enriched for T2D risk variants with altered expression in ER stress. We performed a loss-of-function CRISPR screen for survival under ER stress in EndoC-bH1 cells, which identified 167 pro-survival and 47 pro-death genes involved in processes related to insulin secretion, mitochondrial transport and protein ubiquitination. Beta cell survival genes collectively had limited genomic change in stress yet showed significant, independent enrichment for T2D risk variants, including novel T2D candidate gene DTNB which we validated protects against beta cell death during stress. Overall, our results revealed mediators of ER stress responses in beta cells and identified novel therapeutic targets to preserve beta cells in diabetes pathogenesis.

papers.title: ASD Neuro Agentic (ANA): An Agentic Framework for Feature Discovery and Cross Site Generalization in Autism fMRI Classification
papers.abstract: Classifiers of autism spectrum disorder (ASD) from resting state functional MRI rarely generalize across sites, and many reported accuracies are inflated by data leakage.We show that an agentic artificial intelligence framework, ASD Neuro Agentic (ANA), whose language model agents propose features from the literature and researcher input while fixed tools perform every calculation, can search auditably for site independent classifiers while controlling the leakage. In 1,028 participants from 17 ABIDE I centers, ANA tested 71 pipelines and selected a ComBat harmonized ensemble of tangent space connectivity models from six parcellations and 98 public connectivity derivatives. In leave one center out testing, the ensemble reached an area under the curve of 0.814 (95% CI, 0.773 to 0.841), outperforming ASD DiagNet and ASD SAENet. Predictive connectivity was mainly reduced in ASD. Agentic AI offers a systematic and efficient approach to exploring, evaluating, and identifying pipelines as model selection grows complex.

papers.title: pLM-bVAE: protein language model-enhanced binary representation improves quantum annealing-based protein sequence design
papers.abstract: Quantum annealing (QA) has been explored as an approach for protein design in vast combinatorial sequence spaces. Applying QA to protein sequence design requires amino acid sequences to be encoded as binary vectors, and optimized vectors to be decoded back into amino acid sequences. Thus, both the quality of binary encoding and sequence reconstruction accuracy are important for effective QA-based optimization. Binary variational autoencoder (bVAE) has been used to map protein sequences to binary representations in QA-based protein sequence design. However, bVAE was originally developed for natural language modeling, and its suitability for proteins has not been systematically evaluated. Here, we present pLM-bVAE, which incorporates protein representations derived from a pretrained protein language model (pLM) into the original bVAE model. In computational experiments on three public protein variant datasets, pLM-bVAE showed higher sequence reconstruction accuracy and binary encoding performance than bVAE. Moreover, we incorporated pLM-bVAE into a QA-based protein sequence design framework. Across all three datasets, pLM-bVAE generated more high-scoring sequences with greater sequence dissimilarity from the training and validation data than bVAE. Our results demonstrate that pLM-bVAE provides an effective binary representation for improving QA-based protein sequence design. Availability The source code used in this manuscript is available at https://github.com/hueda8/pLM-bVAE.

papers.title: CPDD: Adapting an autoregressive DNA language model for bidirectional phage genome modeling
papers.abstract: Autoregressive DNA language models generate sequences ef[fi]ciently from left to right, but many genome-analysis and sequence-editing problems are naturally conditioned on both [fl]anks. We introduce CreatiPhage, a 144.5M-parameter autoregressive DNA language model for bacteriophages, and its diffusion extension, CreatiPhage Diffusion DNA-LM (CPDD). CPDD is a 147.5M-parameter bidirectional discrete diffusion model initialized from the six-epoch CreatiPhage checkpoint. CPDD retains the pretrained Transformer, block attention residuals, and Engram conditional memory, while introducing non-causal attention, a MASK-aware base-5 Engram, centered depthwise convolution, and position-aligned nucleotide readout. Training combines masked and GIDD-style uniformly substituted bases with nucleotide- and amino-acid-level losses over a 10 kb, 32 kb, and whole-source context curriculum. On a screened panel of 522 phage CDSs, CPDD achieves higher random-mask restoration accuracy than a comparable diffusion model and performs well above codon-level references. In a mixed-corruption test, it restores 42.4% of visible incorrect bases. Frozen CPDD representations also support infA [fi]tness prediction and seven-class phage virion protein subtype classi[fi]cation. Controlled evaluations further characterize how restoration depends on visible context and identify opportunities to improve longer-range sequence recovery. Together, these results support scaffold-conditioned sequence modeling as a step towards modular design of phage genomes.

papers.title: Multi-Agent Generative Artificial Intelligence for Transfusion Reaction Feature Extraction
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Many transfusion reactions are not reported to hemovigilance systems, and the features needed to recognize them are often documented only in free-text clinical notes. We sought to develop and evaluate an open-source, multi-agent artificial intelligence (AI) pipeline to extract transfusion reaction features defined by the National Healthcare Safety Network (NHSN) Hemovigilance Module from clinical notes. METHODS: We curated 181 features from the NHSN protocol and developed a multi-stage pipeline that extracted features, their timing, and clinical details from free-text notes. Three open-weight large language models (Qwen 3.6-27B, GPT-OSS-120B, and Kimi K3) were applied to 50 notes from expert-written scenarios, published case reports, and MIMIC-IV discharge summaries. Two physicians independently evaluated every model output in a blinded interface. The primary analysis was restricted to feature occurrences with concordant physician assessments. RESULTS: Physicians agreed on 1,201 of 1,343 co-rated feature occurrences (89.4%; Krippendorff's alpha 0.73). Precision was above 0.98 for all models. Sensitivity was 0.774 (95% CI 0.745-0.800) for Kimi K3, 0.636 (0.604-0.667) for GPT-OSS-120B, and 0.624 (0.593-0.655) for Qwen 3.6-27B, and specificity ranged from 0.952 to 0.991. Omissions accounted for more than 94% of false negatives. Timing and clinical details were judged supported or reasonable in more than 92% and 97% of assessments, respectively. Results were consistent across note sources and in analyses including discordant assessments. CONCLUSION: Multi-agent AI pipelines provide a feasible method for extracting transfusion reaction signals from clinical notes with high precision. Our work may have applications in active hemovigilance, reaction classification, and big data research.

papers.title: Human immunodeficiency virus and tuberculosis coinfection prevalence and treatment outcomes in Cameroon: a systematic review and meta-analysis
papers.abstract: Background: Human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) and tuberculosis (TB) form one of the deadliest syndemics, and sub-Saharan Africa bears over 80% of HIV-associated TB deaths. In Cameroon, evidence on HIV/TB coinfection remains unsynthesized across regions and populations, obscuring the national burden. Hence, we estimated the prevalence of HIV/TB coinfection and treatment outcomes in Cameroon. Methods: Following PRISMA 2020 (PROSPERO: CRD420261399169), we searched PubMed, Scopus, Embase, Web of Science, Cochrane Library, African Journals Online, and grey literature for English- and French-language studies conducted in Cameroon. Reports were independently screened, their data extracted, and their methodology appraised using Joanna Briggs Institute tools. Random-effects models pooled prevalence, treatment outcomes, and adjusted odds ratios. Heterogeneity was assessed with I2. Results: Seventy studies (1995-2023) were included, 87.1% at low risk of bias. Pooled HIV prevalence among TB patients was 29.2% (95% CI: 26.3-32.3; 67 studies; n=57,169; I2 = 97.8%), with no significant evidence of publication bias. Prevalence was higher from 2007 onwards (29.9%; 62 studies; n=55,358) than before (20.5%; 5 studies; n=1,811). It was highest in the North-West (41.9%; 7 studies; n=6,324) versus Littoral (25.0%; 15 studies; n=10,419) and West (23.8%; 6 studies; n=4,206); and in extrapulmonary TB (42.3%; 3 studies; n=371) versus mixed forms (37.7%; 21 studies; n=37,239) and pulmonary TB (23.9%; 37 studies; n=16,096) (all p<0.05). Among coinfected patients, pooled treatment success was 75.9% (95% CI: 70.4-80.8; 8 studies; n=4,230), mortality 21.1% (95% CI: 11.9-34.7; 10 studies; n=4,403), loss to follow-up 7.7% (95% CI: 4.3-13.3; 5 studies; n=3,103), and treatment failure 0.3% (95% CI: 0.1-1.5; 6 studies; n=3,520). Lack of antiretroviral therapy (ART) increased the odds of unfavorable outcomes (AOR = 1.90; 95% CI: 1.15-3.12; 2 studies). Conclusions: Approximately three in ten TB patients in Cameroon are coinfected with HIV, with marked regional and clinical variation. Treatment success remains below national targets. Strengthening TB-HIV service integration, routine HIV testing, and timely ART initiation and continuation is essential to reduce the HIV-associated TB morbidity and mortality in the country.

papers.title: Benchmarking Large Language AI Models Against Human Doctors Using an Emergency Medicine Simulation Approach
papers.abstract: Background: Proper adoption of AI in emergency medicine necessitate thorough and rigorous appraisal. Classic benchmarks, which rely heavily on basic question-and-answer formats, though dominating the benchmarking field of LLM usage in medicine, have proven inadequate in assessing the full spectrum of skills incumbent upon an agent in healthcare. Methods: We propose an intricate benchmarking scheme in which the skill set required of an emergency physician is tested and quantified. Our benchmarking structure is 3-fold: skills such as history taking, diagnostic accuracy, treatment plan, and empathy are evaluated by an emergency medicine expert, while the same expertise is scored by an intern from the perspective of a patient, through what we call a simulated emergency room visit. A comprehensive written examination is also utilized to measure general emergency medicine knowledge. Results: Eight LLMs were benchmarked against each other and in contrast to nine emergency medical doctors. Our findings indicate that the AI models significantly outperformed human physicians across several key domains, including history taking, investigation, diagnostic accuracy, and treatment planning. Furthermore, the models demonstrated superior performance in comprehensibility, credibility, and empathy. When comparing AI models against each other, performance advantages were marginal during simulated emergency room visits and were mostly pronounced during the written examination. Conclusion: AI models demonstrate a clear advantage over human physicians across a diverse range of emergency medicine competencies. The proposed benchmarking scheme provides a comprehensive metric for a thorough evaluation of medical skill set, furthering validation, adaptation, and utilization of AI in emergency medicine.

papers.title: Myeloid subpopulations correlate with responsiveness to therapy in a prospective, longitudinal study on RA patients
papers.abstract: Background: Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is an autoimmune disease associated with the destruction of cartilage and bone, increased risk of cardiovascular disease and a higher mortality rate. Despite the many therapies that exist for RA, there is little information to guide selection of the most effective treatment for an individual patient. Ultrasound-guided synovial biopsies have created an opportunity to investigate the target tissue. While a number of studies have characterized the stromal and immune cell populations using single-cell technology on synovial biopsy samples, here we performed a longitudinal study, where we collected comprehensive clinical data over a one-year period on each patient in the process of changing their therapy. Methods: Samples from minimally invasive, ultrasound-guided synovial biopsies were collected from RA patients at baseline prior to start of a new therapy and 4-6-week follow-up under IRB-approved protocols with informed consent. Comprehensive clinical data from each appointment were recorded into a shared REDCap database. Failure to respond to therapy was based on clinical disease activity index (CDAI) for RA after 12-18 weeks post therapy. Biopsied samples were dissociated, enriched for CD45 or CD45CD11b cells, and processed on the 10X Genomics Chromium platform to generate libraries for single-cell RNA sequencing with cell-surface protein detection (CITE-seq). Spatial transcriptomics were performed on formalin-fixed paraffin embedded sections analyzed with 10X Xenium and NanoString CosMx. Results: We performed CITE-seq analysis on ~38,000 CD45+ synovial cells isolated from 17 patients who failed a conventional or biologic DMARD and planned to change therapy. We then subclustered on the myeloid population to reveal 12 myeloid subpopulations that consist of macrophages (n = 8), Osteoclast-like cells, DCs (n = 2) and proliferating cells. The proportion of cDCs was significantly higher in responders, while the proportion of macrophages was significantly lower in responders. The proportion of ISG15+ and THBS1+macrophages were enriched in the non-responder patients. Spatial transcriptomics revealed that ISG15+ macrophages were preferentially localized to the synovial lining, while the THBS1+ macrophages are likely interacting with lymphoid cells within the sublining tissue. Conclusions: These data are among the first to prospectively profile macrophage populations as predictors of response to therapy. Future studies are required to verify whether myeloid subpopulation associations hold across specific therapies.

papers.title: Applications of Fairness Training in Artificial Intelligence to Ophthalmic Disease Diagnosis using External Eye Photographs
papers.abstract: Diabetic retinopathy (DR), age-related macular degeneration (AMD), and glaucoma are leading causes of preventable blindness, yet whether external eye photographs carry phenotypic information about posterior segment disease remains unclear, and methods to mitigate demographic disparities in such models are largely unexplored. We developed and evaluated deep learning and vision-language models for binary classification of vision-threatening DR (VTDR), advanced AMD, and glaucoma using 40,687 external eye photographs from 9,878 patients at Massachusetts Eye and Ear. Convolutional networks (WResNet, EfficientNet), a vision transformer (ViT), and a fine-tuned vision-language model (LLaVA) were assessed by area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), with fairness across sex, race, and ethnicity quantified by the equity-scaled AUC (ES-AUC). Five fairness-training strategies were applied to the best models. LLaVA achieved the highest baseline AUC for VTDR (85.4%, comparable to ViT 82.6%); advanced AMD was similar across architectures (EfficientNet 86.3%; LLaVA 84.8%; ViT 84.7%), whereas glaucoma was substantially worse (67-74%). Fairness training improved VTDR and AMD AUCs to 86.3% and 85.9% while partially mitigating demographic disparities. In summary, although AI models that rely on external eye photography to detect posterior segment disease may not yet be suitable for clinical deployment, the fairness methods demonstrated in this proof-of-concept study could be applied to other AI systems to decrease performance disparities and potentially improve model performance.

papers.title: Agentic Pipeline for Large-Scale Clinical Data Queries in Enterprise Electronic Health Records
papers.abstract: Using electronic health record (EHR) data to answer clinical research questions is challenging. It requires understanding the research question, finding relevant information across different sources, and combining that information to produce meaningful results. We developed an agentic large language model (LLM) pipeline that decomposes investigator-authored requests into source-specific tasks, generates and executes SQL on EHR, integrates structured and unstructured EHR evidence, and applies study-specific clinical note adjudication. We evaluated this workflow against data analyst-identified cohorts across 50 pediatric orthopedic clinical data query requests. Of these, 43 were included in manual-review-adjusted performance analyses. The median adjusted positive predictive value, sensitivity among patients identified by either approach, and corresponding F1 score were 0.93 (95% CI, 0.88-0.98), 0.92 (95% CI, 0.90-0.95) and 0.90 (95% CI, 0.87-0.94), respectively. These findings support the feasibility of translating natural-language research intent into executable, autonomous multi-stage EHR workflows.

papers.title: LLM Embeddings Complement Theory-Driven Language Features and Cognitive Scores for APOE4 and Aβ Prediction
papers.abstract: Spontaneous language offers a scalable, noninvasive approach for identifying biological indicators of preclinical Alzheimer's disease (AD). We examined prediction of APOE4 carrier status and cerebral amyloid-beta burden using Cookie Theft picture descriptions from two cohorts of Hebrew- and English-speaking participants (IRAP, N=134; WRAP, N=1,541). Amyloid-beta burden was classified using lowest-quartile, median, and highest-quartile cutoffs, capturing accumulation below conventional amyloid-positivity thresholds. We compared embeddings from pretrained large language models (LLMs) with standard cognitive test scores, reflecting conventional clinical assessment, and theory-driven linguistic features, reflecting traditional language analysis. Embedding-based models achieved the highest F1 scores among constituent models in five of eight tasks involving APOE4 status and global amyloid-beta burden. High prediction disagreement suggested complementary signals across approaches. An any-positive ensemble significantly outperformed every constituent model and a prior-informed random baseline across all eight tasks, and significantly outperformed all constituent models in 21 of 24 regional amyloid-beta tasks. These findings highlight the complementarity of LLM-based, theory-driven, and cognitive measures for predicting AD-related genetic risk and amyloid pathology, and support further investigation of their potential for early screening approaches.

papers.title: The LAMp-LC Study: Unveiling the lung microbiome in Australians with early- and late-stage lung cancer using shotgun metagenomics
papers.abstract: Lung cancer remains the leading cause of cancer-related mortality, yet the role of lower airway microbiota in disease development and progression is incompletely defined. Here, we characterised the lung microbiome in an Australian cohort (lung cancer n=106, healthy n=10) using shotgun metagenomics and semi-quantitative culture to evaluate site-specific microbial ecology across the tumour microenvironment (TME), contralateral airways, and oral cavity, to evaluate microbiome differences across early- and late-stage disease, and to quantify clinical covariate impacts on airway microbiota. Diversity analyses, multivariable linear modelling, and culture-based comparisons were performed, with adjustment for smoking pack-years, sex, and tumour characteristics. Cumulative smoking exposure caused significant, progressive core commensal depletion (Neisseria subflava, Gemella sanguinis, Rothia mucilaginosa), alongside Streptococcus mitis enrichment, with Mogibacterium diversum uniquely depleted within the TME of smokers. {beta} diversity in both early- and late-stage bronchial washes (BWs) significantly diverged from healthy controls, whilst Shannon diversity ( diversity) was significantly reduced in early-stage compared with late-stage BWs. The early-stage TME also demonstrated significantly reduced microbial cultivability compared with healthy and other lung cancer BWs. A small number of taxa were uniquely enriched (Sporothrix and Pseudomonas species) or depleted (Streptococcus parasanguinis, Streptococcus cristatus, R. mucilaginosa) within the TME, and 13 taxa were significantly enriched or depleted in both TME and contralateral airways compared with healthy airways. Only lung adenocarcinoma showed distinct oral {beta}-diversity restructuring. Taken together, our findings demonstrate that the lung cancer microbiome is characterised by early and progressive lower airway dysbiosis that is strongly shaped by tumour presence. Our findings point to potential new avenues for microbiome-based diagnostic and therapeutic strategies.
